text:
sophie-cs: Hey team, Lyra (onboarding) hit a bunch of 429s in APAC this morning during their demo. Customer asks for a short-term rate bump + allowlist while we debug routing. Renewal conversation next week so we want zero friction. :grimacing:
marco-ops: Noted. Can we give specifics on which endpoints and IP ranges?
sophie-cs: They're hitting text-generation and embeddings — mostly /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings from three CIDRs: 203.22.10.0/24, 203.22.11.0/24, 45.77.120.0/22. Demo traffic spike spiked qps from 5→120.
jess-infra: Ok. For temporary relief we can do: - APAC edge peering priority + regional fallback to sin-1 - temp rate window increase from 5→120 qps for 72h - add the CIDRs to allowlist. I'll need a ticket and approval from security for the IPs.
anya-eng: Quick note — their model pin is rwd-13b-v2-quant, which has lower throughput per GPU. Suggest we route their demo traffic to an autoscaled pool with slightly higher instance counts rather than switching model. Avoiding model variant fallback keeps quality consistent for their demo.
liam-sales: Sophie — can you confirm the timeframe they want? Sales wants to avoid overcommitting. Also flagging renewal touch: if we nail this demo, renewal likely positive. If they keep hitting errors it's a risk.
sophie-cs: They requested immediate increase for the next 48 hours, demo at 2024-11-05T03:00Z. Prefer autorevoke after 72h. I'll draft a formal request.
marco-ops: I'll open infra ticket: INFRA-8421. Patch plan: add CIDRs to allowlist (apac-edge-peers), update rate_window in routing-config for lyra-corp to 120 qps with ttl 259200 (72h). Sample config:
```json
{"customer_id":"lyra-corp","route":"apac-primary","rate_limit_qps":120,"allowlist":["203.22.10.0/24","203.22.11.0/24","45.77.120.0/22"],"ttl_seconds":259200}
```
marco-ops: tagging @jess-infra for the peering priority change and @ops-bot for audit log entry.
ops-bot: Audit entry created: ticket=INFRA-8421, actor=marco-ops, change=allowlist+rate-window, ttl=259200s. :white_check_mark:
jess-infra: I can do peering priority and edge routing change. Will need a quick security thumbs-up for the CIDRs. @sophie-cs can you confirm these are customer-owned IPs?
sophie-cs: Confirmed — Lyra provided a signed IP ownership doc. Uploading to the ticket now.
anya-eng: I'll add a temporary canary split: 10% of Lyra traffic goes to the autoscaled pool for 30m to validate latency/kv-cache interactions, then ramp if stable. I'll monitor the token latencies.
marco-ops: After canary success we'll flip to 100% for the 48h demo window and then autorevoke per TTL. I'll also add a soft-alert to eng-sre if 5xx or 95p latency > 800ms.
liam-sales: Great. Sophie, can you capture the customer's post-demo feedback on perceived latency and any prompt regressions? We'll attach to renewal notes.
sophie-cs: Will do. I'll also ask them for sample failing prompts to add to our evals suite.
jess-infra: Security pre-approves; moving to staging then prod. ETA ~20m.
marco-ops: Updated INFRA-8421 with config and TTL. Pushing to prod now — will post final confirmation. :rocket:
marco-ops: Done. Allowlist + rate_window applied. Canary started (10%). Monitoring.
ops-bot: Canary metrics: error_rate=0.6%, p95_latency=420ms — within SLO.
anya-eng: Canary looks healthy, ramping to 100% over 5m.
marco-ops: Ramp complete. Temp rate_window active. Autorevoke scheduled at +72h. Manual rollback instructions in ticket.
sophie-cs: LYRA confirmed demo succeeded and pinged product team for follow-up. They're happy with latency. I'll add notes to renewal tracker and hand to Liam for the renewal call. :tada:
